answer.label: Condensed from
answer.sourceLine: Le Guin made this argument in her National Book Foundation medal speech on 19 November 2014. The official transcript includes “but then” before the comparison with kings; the displayed version is a familiar condensation of her own words.

author.name: Ursula K. Le Guin
author.heading: About Ursula K. Le Guin
author.bio: Ursula K. Le Guin wrote speculative fiction that used imagined societies to examine power, gender and the ways people live together. Her books include A Wizard of Earthsea, The Left Hand of Darkness and The Dispossessed; her essays also defended imagination as an adult responsibility.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: Accepting a lifetime-achievement medal, Le Guin warned against confusing literature with a market commodity. Her comparison with divine-right monarchy makes capitalism historically changeable, while the speech presents imaginative writing as one place where alternatives can begin.
